page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier. It achieves a PassMark CPU score of 19,335.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,756.0. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,435.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,851.77. The primary architectural tradeoff is the highly constrained memory capacity of 16.0 GB for a 16-vCPU allocation. While memory bandwidth is decent at 99.23 GB/sec for large block reads, memory-intensive tasks or large-scale databases will face severe resource bottlenecks. This is reflected in LLM inference benchmarks, where a medium 7B model drops to a weak 31.77 tokens/sec for prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.u1-c1m1.4xlarge offers a high density of dedicated compute cores relative to its memory footprint, making it a cost-effective choice for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory allocations. It is well-suited for parallelizable, compute-heavy tasks such as software compilation, where it scores 14,936.0 on Geekbench, as well as text processing, static web serving, and lightweight multi-threaded decompression. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data science, or heavy LLM inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-focused server instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a low 1:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, but provides a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place its performance in the average tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 19,335.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,756.0. While it delivers solid performance for parallelized CPU tasks like software compilation and text processing, the 16.0 GB memory limit presents a significant tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for compute-heavy, low-memory workloads such as static web serving, lightweight multi-threaded decompression, and parallelized build pipelines.
